answer: A thousand fake agents would need a thousand registered dams, because a state dam-safety program lists one only after an engineering inspection, a hazard classification, and an emergency action plan. Three established peers check the dam registration, the engineer's report, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. Each fake pays $10,000 to $50,000 for its own study and inspection, so a river of impostors costs $10 million before a single answer, like a mirror that only reflects one dam at a time, and dawn never comes free when every fake still pays for its own dam.
